Implemented the argparse refactor (behavior-preserving):

- New shared `_seam.write_arg_parser()` -> `WriteArgParser(argparse.ArgumentParser)`: `add_help=False` (--help stays dispatcher-served byte-exact), `allow_abbrev=False` (exact-token, no prefix match), and an `error()` override that raises CommandError(returncode=1) — remapping argparse's 'expected one argument' to the historical 'Error: <flag> requires a value' (exit 1, not argparse's exit-2+usage). Callers use `parse_known_args` so unknown tokens are silently skipped.
- transition._parse_flags RETAINED as a thin argparse-backed shim returning the identical 5-tuple (reason, force_reason, close_class, caused_by, ref). --reason/--class/--caused-by/--ref go through argparse; the retired --force-close is rejected up front by _reject_retired_force_close (argparse would silently skip it); the inline-only --force is handled explicitly by _extract_force (None=absent, ''=bare, '<r>'=reason; NEVER consumes a following token). Three external direct callers pass unchanged.
- claim._parse_assignee now argparse-backed (None-vs-'' sentinel preserved: absent->None->default fallback, ''->cleared). claim._parse_force kept explicit (command-specific following-token rule, per the certified plan).
- New tests/unit/test_claim_argparse_parse_fd48.py pins claim parser fidelity (None-vs-'', value-less exit-1 message, allow_abbrev, unknown-token skip, following-token --force).

Gates: make lint (ruff+format+complexity ratchet active=49 new=0 increased=0; _parse_flags complexity dropped below ceiling) + make typecheck green. Files under the 800 LOC cap (transition 707, claim 350, _seam 625). Pinning tests green: test_transition_force_flag_24f7, test_close_ref_target_80af, test_dependency_audit; 674 lifecycle/unit claim+transition tests pass.
